receiptMedia.font: Receipt/export only: public/fonts/SpecialElite-Regular.ttf, Apache-2.0 license in public/fonts/SpecialElite-LICENSE.txt; page and export controls retain Buenard.
receiptMedia.presentation: Permanent ISO issue instant and random non-immediately-repeating stamp captured with the chosen reading. America/New_York printed date; cloned presentation and cached PNG stay identical across midnight.
receiptMedia.provenance: 44 shipping public/art PNGs scanned, zero missing provenance records. Stamp sources/prompts: assets/receipt-concepts/stamp-generations-v2.json. share-panorama.png copies approved sky-panorama.png; v3 approval comps retained as history. Stamp preparation recipes: assets/receipt-concepts/stamp-crops.json. Source paper pixels verified identical; panorama copy bytes verified identical.
receiptMedia.socialProvenance: Archival assets/receipt-art/social-icons.png and social-icons.json preserve original exact prompt, source identity and crop recipe. The Share panel and three derived public/art/social icons were removed.
receiptMedia.toolbarReview: Historical share-toolbar-finish-review.md records the superseded panel implementation; no longer current UI authority.
receiptMedia.pageTools: Download and Copy occupy the receipt’s upper-right, anchored within the narrow top edge of the flared paper at right 24% and top 6px, in a named “Save your fortune” group. Two 44px square buttons contain authored 22px native SVGs, accessible names and above-control hover/focus tooltips. About remains alone at the page upper-right at every width. Both start disabled with “Get a fortune first” tooltips, enable after an actual issue and disable during issuing or an export operation. There is no Share button, platform panel, social-network action or native-sharing path. A polite status region follows the receipt in document flow, centered at a maximum width of 360px with 20px side padding and 15px Buenard at line height 1.4; it disappears when empty. Download prepares the cached PNG as `cosmic-bullshit-fortune.png` and announces that it is ready to save. Copy retains the chosen title when applicable, full reading, real/invented label, brand and homepage URL; success explicitly identifies the link as the homepage. Failures offer retry or the other action. Clipboard availability depends on browser permissions.
receiptMedia.opening: The opening paper reads “Bad Day?” followed by one of six questions from `src/lib/intro-questions.ts`. Initialization chooses once per page load; these prompts never enter the issued-reading catalog. The Moon version asks “Has the Moon put your motivation on airplane mode?” The introductory classification is empty and hidden; “Before we begin” is absent. Classification becomes visible on issue. The opening has generic invented artwork, no issued stamp/date and no exportable selection. A normal request replaces it with the chosen fortune, classification, artwork and frozen presentation.
receiptMedia.copyPadding: 64px top padding at every width clears receipt-corner controls; prior 10% and 74px treatments are historical.
receiptMedia.pageToolsReview: Historical page-tools-finish-review.md records the superseded header placement and opening label; no longer current UI authority.
receiptMedia.receiptCornerReview: receipt-corner-finish-review.md: SHIP for requested correction, no material fixes. Twelve intro/issued captures at six widths independently inspected. Parent reports 48 passing tests, zero check diagnostics, successful build, browser download/copy/frozen-midnight/error-recovery checks. Detector advisories only. Historical whole-page gate remains open. User authorized pushing corrected work; completed push/deployment is not claimed.

narrative.overview:
Cosmic Bullshit feels like an old printed amusement made operational: warm ochre paper, plum engraving, worn brass, and an exhausted but charming clerk. The illustration carries the ornate personality; the surrounding interface stays readable and spare. The humor is warm, absurd, and plainly entertainment.

This document records the implemented system in `src/pages/index.astro`, `src/pages/license.astro`, `src/styles/home.css`, `src/styles/receipt.css`, and `src/scripts/fortune-machine.ts`. It describes code authority, not a whole-page finish verdict. The user approved the taller production cabinet during asset review; the original decision comp retains shorter geometry. The receipt extension has a scoped local-review verdict; historical whole-page comparison and plate concerns remain open and are not converted into design rules.
keyCharacteristics: Warm printed material and plum ink.
Locally hosted Buenard for the page and SpecialElite for receipt/export text.
Illustrated depth with real HTML text and controls.
Mostly still character performance with deliberate comic pauses.
Clear separation between factual sky events and invented excuses.

rules.name: The Ink and Paper Rule
rules.body: Use plum text on the warm paper ground for ordinary content; reserve vermilion for the primary action.

rules.name: The Material Depth Rule
rules.body: Add depth where an object physically meets another surface; keep ordinary text content on the paper ground.

rules.name: The Growing Paper Rule
rules.body: Let the live receipt grow to preserve all title and reading text at its established readable size; never shrink the reading to fit a decorative plate.

rules.name: The Still First Rule
rules.body: Keep the clerk still most of the time; animate one restrained gesture only after a random 15–30 second pause or a user request.

dos: Do preserve warm paper, plum ink, and restrained vermilion action.
Do keep text and interaction in live HTML above the illustration.
Do preserve the clerk's identity, steady lighting, fixed window, and long still pauses.
Do retain visible factual-versus-invented labels, keyboard focus, motion preferences, and asset provenance.
Do let the receipt grow for the full chosen reading and use the same frozen selection for download and copy.
donts: Don't replace the illustration's material depth with generic floating cards.
Don't bake changing fortune text or the interactive action label into artwork.
Don't shrink live reading text, clamp content, or use the homepage preview as a selected-fortune image.
Don't turn unresolved plate edges, crop drift, or old-comp geometry differences into reusable design rules.
Don't describe this documentation or the taller-cabinet approval as a closed finish review.
